Will it work with Magento upgrades?

We build using Magento's extension points and avoid core edits, which is the best protection against upgrade problems. Major version upgrades can still need small changes, and we note which parts to test.
Can you fix or extend a third-party extension?
We can add features through plugins and overrides in a separate module, or fix small bugs in code you own. Editing a paid vendor extension directly can break its updates and license, so we avoid it.
Can you publish my module on the Marketplace?
We can prepare it to Marketplace standards, but Adobe reviews submissions and we cannot promise acceptance. Our price covers building the module for your store.
desc:
Custom Magento extension development adds the exact feature your store is missing, without bending core code or buying a bulky package. Ecom Swift LLC builds clean Magento modules with an admin setting page, tests them on staging and hands over the code.

## What is a custom Magento extension?

A custom Magento extension, also called a module, is a self-contained package of code that adds a feature to your store. It might add a product option, a delivery date picker, an admin report, an order export, a loyalty scheme or a link to another system. Magento loads it through Composer, and it can be switched on or off from the admin.

A good module does one job and stays out of the way of everything else in your store.

## Why a custom module can beat a ready-made one

Marketplace extensions are built for the average store, so they carry settings and code you will never use. Some add extra database queries to every page. Others clash with another extension that touches the same part of checkout.

When your need is specific, a small custom module is often lighter and easier to maintain. It does what your process requires, and you own the logic. The trade-off is that someone must write it carefully, which is why coding standards, tests and documentation matter.

## How a well-built module affects your store

A module affects results through time saved and errors avoided. An order export that runs by itself replaces hours of copying data into a spreadsheet. A delivery date picker removes phone calls about when parcels arrive. A custom option on a product page lets buyers order personalized items without sending emails.

It also affects performance and risk. Poorly written code can slow pages or break after an upgrade. Code that follows Magento standards uses plugins and observers, so core files stay untouched and upgrades remain possible.

## What a great Magento extension includes

- A single clear purpose, written down before coding starts.
- Plugins, observers and dependency injection instead of core edits.
- An admin settings page to enable, disable and configure the feature.
- Its own database table when the data needs one, created through proper setup scripts.
- A storefront block, template or API endpoint that outputs the result.
- Admin grids or reports with filters and permissions where relevant.
- Cron jobs or message queues for heavy tasks, so pages stay quick.
- Automated tests for the main logic in the larger packages.
- Installation through Composer, so deployment is repeatable.
- A short usage guide and commented source code.

## How we build it

We start with a brief conversation or a short written spec: who uses the feature, what triggers it and what the result should be. We then agree the scope, so both sides know what is included.

We develop on a staging copy of your store, install the module the same way it will be installed live and test it with your real product types. We check it alongside your existing extensions and your theme. After your approval, we install it on the live store and hand over the source code and a usage note.

The Basic package covers one small module with an on and off switch. The Standard package covers a mid-size module with an admin page, its own table and a storefront output or endpoint. The Premium package covers up to three linked modules, with REST or GraphQL endpoints, cron jobs, tests and a period of fixes.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the problem you want solved, not only the feature you imagine.
- Give us example orders, products or files the module will handle.
- Keep a backup before each install.
- Test the module on staging whenever you upgrade Magento.
- Store the source in your own repository.

**Avoid:**
- Asking one module to do many unrelated jobs.
- Editing core Magento files to save time.
- Installing code from unknown sources next to your own module.
- Skipping the staging test on a busy store.
- Leaving the code undocumented.

## Who it is for

This service suits a store owner whose warehouse needs a specific order export format, which no marketplace extension provides. It also suits a business that sells made-to-order goods and needs custom product options. A third case is a company that wants Magento to talk to an internal tool through a small endpoint.

## What we need from you

Send a plain description of the feature, any example files or screens and the Magento version you run. We also need staff, collaborator or developer access to your admin and a staging copy, or we can help you create one. We never ask for passwords, and the finished module is handed over for you to use in your store.
